title: Hosea Bible Quiz - Chapter 6
description: Ten questions on Hosea 6: the call to return to Yahweh, love like a morning cloud, and mercy desired more than sacrifice.

questions.text: What reason does the opening call give for returning to Yahweh?
questions.explanation: The verse says he has torn us to pieces and he will heal us, he has injured us and he will bind up our wounds.

answers.text: He has forgotten us and he will remember us
He has torn us to pieces and he will heal us
He has sold us and he will buy us back
He has hidden from us and he will appear to us

questions.text: What does this chapter say will happen after two days and on the third day?
questions.explanation: The verse says after two days he will revive us, and on the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.

answers.text: He will gather us and lead us up out of Egypt
He will judge us and divide the land again
He will send rain and fill the threshing floors
He will revive us and raise us up, and we will live before him

questions.text: What is Yahweh coming compared with in the opening call?
questions.explanation: The verse says that as surely as the sun rises Yahweh will appear, and that he will come like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.

answers.text: Like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth
Like a fire that burns up the stubble of the field
Like a whirlwind that sweeps away the threshing floor
Like a shepherd who gathers the lambs in his arms

questions.text: What is the love of Ephraim and Judah compared with?
questions.explanation: The verse says their love is like a morning cloud and like the dew that disappears early.

answers.text: A broken cistern and a dry riverbed
A fading flower and withered grass
A morning cloud and dew that disappears early
A sealed spring and a locked garden

questions.text: With what does Yahweh say he has cut them to pieces?
questions.explanation: The verse says he has cut them to pieces with the prophets and killed them with the words of his mouth.

answers.text: With the sword, and with the bow of the enemy
With the prophets, and with the words of his mouth
With famine, and with the drought of summer
With the nations, and with the kings of the north

questions.text: What does Yahweh say he desires, and what does he desire more than burnt offerings?
questions.explanation: The verse says he desires mercy and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

answers.text: Vows rather than silver, and a clean house
Fasting rather than feasting, and quiet hearts
Justice rather than tribute, and a strong city
Mercy rather than sacrifice, and the knowledge of God

questions.text: Whom are they compared with in breaking the covenant?
questions.explanation: The verse says that they, like Adam, have broken the covenant and were unfaithful to him there.

answers.text: Adam
Jacob
Jehu
Esau

questions.text: What does this chapter say about Gilead?
questions.explanation: The verse says Gilead is a city of those who work iniquity, and that it is stained with blood.

answers.text: It is a city of refuge for those who flee
It is a city of priests who serve at the altar
It is a city of those who work iniquity, stained with blood
It is a city of merchants who weigh out silver

questions.text: What does the chapter say the company of priests do on the path toward Shechem?
questions.explanation: The verse says that as gangs of robbers wait to ambush a man, so the company of priests murder on the path toward Shechem, committing shameful crimes.

answers.text: They beg for bread, like travellers without a home
They murder, like gangs of robbers waiting to ambush
They burn incense, like watchmen on the hills
They collect tribute, like servants of the king

questions.text: What does Yahweh say he has seen in the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: The verse says that in the house of Israel he has seen a horrible thing, that there is prostitution in Ephraim and Israel is defiled.

answers.text: An empty altar and a silent harp
A broken wall and an open gate
A sealed book and a hidden vision
A horrible thing, prostitution in Ephraim
